newsitem.title: FRANCE: Annan to urge U.N. force for Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Annan to urge U.N. force for Zaire.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Friday he hoped to persuade member states to reconsider sending a multinational force to eastern Zaire in the light of what he called a very serious humanitarian situation.

"I hope with this information we can persuade member states to reconsider the decision to cancel the multinational force for eastern Zaire," Annan told reporters after talks with French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette.

Annan said he had no precise information about reported massacres of Rwandan Hutu refugees in the area where Tutsi rebels are fighting against Zaire government forces but he said "the humanitarian situation is very serious".

He said that the international community had not shown a sufficient political will to send the force created by a U.N. resolution last year but he would take the issue up again on his return to New York.
De Charette said France expressed its grave concern at the humanitarian situation in eastern Zaire which made an immediate halt to fighting essential.
He called for an international investigation into reports of abuses in the region, adding "this is a matter of great urgency".
